questions.question: To be economically "marginalised" means:
options: Held at the margin of the economy — shut out of ownership, formal employment, skills, credit and decision-making
Earning slightly less than a colleague
Working in the informal sector by choice
Living outside a metropolitan area

questions.question: South African marginalisation is described as "the intended product of laws" because:
options: Markets failed on their own without state involvement
Exclusion from land, residence, schooling and occupations was written into statute by design
The laws were badly drafted accidents
Only informal customs excluded people

questions.question: Black women are said to have "carried both exclusions at once" because they faced:
options: Only the exclusions applied to women
Only the exclusions applied to Black South Africans
Racial exclusion plus legal and customary bars on property, contracts and credit, plus unpaid care work limiting the hours they could sell
No legal exclusion, only market discrimination

questions.question: The intersection point — the young woman with a disability in a remote village — teaches that:
options: Each barrier waits its turn and is faced separately
Categories of disadvantage never overlap
Disability is the only barrier that matters economically
Overlapping categories COMPOUND into a single multiplied wall of exclusion

subtopics.title: Redress Through the Factors of Production

questions.question: The three tracks of land reform are:
options: Restitution for post-1913 dispossession, redistribution for those never permitted to own, and tenure reform securing insecure occupation
Purchase, auction and inheritance
Fencing, irrigation and titling
Leasing, rezoning and taxation

questions.question: "Transfer plus support is redress; transfer alone is a ceremony" means:
options: Land transfers should be celebrated publicly
A transferred hectare without finance, equipment, training and a route to a buyer produces neither income nor output
Ceremonial transfers are legally invalid
Support should replace transfer entirely

questions.question: Employment equity law targets management and professional levels in particular because:
options: Junior posts are exempt from the law
Managers are cheaper to recruit
That is where exclusion bit hardest — and where decisions are made
Unions demanded it in wage talks

questions.question: In the CAPITAL factor, redress operates through:
options: Minimum wages and leave entitlements
Land titling alone
Import tariffs on machinery
B-BBEE ownership stakes, management representation, supplier development and preferential procurement, plus development finance for those without collateral

questions.question: Labour legislation counts as democratisation because it:
options: Turns workers from people decisions happen TO into people decisions are negotiated WITH
Lets workers set company strategy alone
Abolishes the employment contract
Transfers firms to state ownership

questions.question: The four constituencies seated at NEDLAC are:
options: The courts, the police, the treasury and the central bank
Government, organised business, organised labour and organised community
Provinces, municipalities, banks and exporters
Employers, consumers, importers and farmers

questions.question: NEDLAC's defining feature is that:
options: It passes economic legislation itself
It hears individual retrenchment disputes
Major labour legislation and significant economic policy are negotiated there BEFORE reaching Parliament — consensus through social dialogue
It sets the annual budget

questions.question: The honest limit of the NEDLAC model is that:
options: Business refuses to attend
Its agreements have no legal effect
It meets only in election years
Consensus is slow, and a constituency only speaks as loudly as it is organised — the weakly organised are quietest

questions.question: The consistent macro-economic aims framing redress are:
options: Performance, employment, equitable distribution, internal stability and external stability
Zero taxation and zero borrowing
Fixed exchange rates and price freezes
Maximum exports at any cost

questions.question: "Policy IS the trade-off" captures the tension that:
options: All aims can be maximised simultaneously with good management
Redistribution needs revenue, revenue needs growth, growth may reward existing capital, and stability disciplines the borrowing social programmes would need
Stability and growth are the same objective
Employment targets make other aims unnecessary

questions.question: The measurable ACHIEVEMENTS ledger of redress includes:
options: The elimination of inequality
Land reform completed ahead of target
Millions connected to water, electricity and housing; grants holding back destitution; a large Black professional class; shifted ownership and management; new rights and institutions
Unemployment reduced to negligible levels

questions.question: The phrase "broad-based" entered the empowerment legislation in response to the criticism that:
options: Empowerment moved too quickly
Too many small firms benefited
The programme taxed the poor
Benefits had sometimes pooled among a connected few rather than spreading widely

subtopics.title: Starting the Race at Different Lines

questions.question: The two job applicants — one with a car, home printing and an uncle who knows the manager; one with two borrowed taxi fares and no contacts — illustrate:
options: The same post reached from very different starting lines drawn by history
That interviews reward effort alone
That transport is irrelevant to opportunity
That contacts play no role in hiring

questions.question: The starting lines were drawn by:
options: Random differences in talent
Laws deciding who could own a house, whose school got laboratories, who lived near the factories, and who could trade on the main road
Weather patterns and geography alone
Individual spending choices

questions.question: "Scrapping the rules did not scrap their results" because:
options: The rules remain in force today
Results and rules are unrelated
The unowned house still cannot be borrowed against, the untaught trade still cannot be passed on, and the far address is still far — advantage and disadvantage are inherited
The economy resets each generation automatically

subtopics.title: Four Things You Need to Build a Livelihood

questions.question: Naledi's family plot, worked for two generations without a title deed, is directly addressed by:
options: Redistribution
Tenure reform — converting insecure occupation into rights the law defends
Restitution
Preferential procurement

questions.question: The skills leg of Naledi's livelihood is rebuilt through:
options: Import quotas on eggs
A ceiling on poultry prices
Levy-funded learnerships, apprenticeships and technical training, with employment equity opening jobs up to management level
A grant paid instead of training

questions.question: The loan officer says no because Naledi's family owns nothing a bank recognises; redress answers with:
options: Instructing banks to abolish interest
Advising her to save for thirty years first
Closing commercial banks
Ownership channels plus finance designed for people without collateral — development funders and small-business schemes

questions.question: The single test to apply to any redress programme is:
options: Did it hand over an object, or leave behind a working livelihood?
Did it cost less than the alternative?
Was it announced by a senior official?
Did it reach the news?

questions.question: A municipality calling residents' meetings before setting next year's spending, and a regulator inviting objections before a tariff increase, are examples of:
options: Self-regulation by professionals
Public participation — those affected by economic decisions given a channel into them
Collective bargaining
Preferential procurement

questions.question: Big economic laws "stop at the NEDLAC table before travelling to Parliament" so that:
options: Parliament can be bypassed permanently
Ministers can avoid accountability
The arguments happen early, among the people who will live with the outcome — deliberately slower, by design
Laws can be kept confidential

questions.question: Self-regulation by engineers, doctors and accountants means:
options: These professions operate outside any law
Government writes their daily codes of practice
Their standards are set by popular vote
Practitioners police their own professional standards inside a legal framework, with public accountability so it does not decay into self-protection

questions.question: "Write both columns with the mechanisms attached and you are doing economics; write only one and you are doing propaganda" instructs you to:
options: State real gains AND real shortfalls of redress, each explained by its mechanism
List achievements only, to stay positive
List shortfalls only, to stay critical
Avoid the topic as too political
